statement: Write lower(w) for the byte vector obtained from w by replacing every byte c with 65 <= c <= 90 by c+32 and leaving every other byte unchanged. Write vn(w) for the byte vector of the same length with vn(w)[p] = 0 if lower(w)[p] is one of 97,101,105,111,117 (the lowercase vowels a,e,i,o,u), and vn(w)[p] = lower(w)[p] otherwise. Byte-vector equality is exact string equality; [] is the empty byte vector. The function returns a result r, len(r)=len(queries), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), writing q=queries[i], r[i] is determined by the following precedence: (1) if there exists j with wordlist[j]=q, then r[i]=q; (2) otherwise, if there exists j with lower(wordlist[j])=lower(q), then r[i]=wordlist[j0] where j0 is the least such j; (3) otherwise, if there exists j with vn(wordlist[j])=vn(q), then r[i]=wordlist[j0] where j0 is the least such j; (4) otherwise r[i]=[].
preconditions: len(wordlist) >= 1 and len(queries) >= 1 and len(wordlist) <= 5000 and len(queries) <= 5000; each wordlist[j] and queries[i] is a nonempty byte vector of length at most 7 whose bytes are ASCII letters (65-90 or 97-122).
